coarse_skill_concept: Building C/C++/Fortran software from source using cmake or make, including updating compiler flags, adding cross-compilation toolchain targets, or fixing stale build rules.

task_judgments.reason: cmake is used for one sub-step (building OpenCV from source), but the dominant challenges are fixing a pybind11 API incompatibility in bindings.cpp and wiring up a Python package install from a local path—neither of which belongs to the cmake/make diagnosis loop.
Exactly matches the skill: read the Makefile, identify the wrong compiler (ifort) and stale flag (-fast), patch with sed, and rebuild with make.

Requires patching the Makefile to add a MIPS cross-compilation toolchain (CC, LLVM_TARGET, MIPS_AS/LD, flags), then invoking make—exactly the cross-compilation toolchain targeting sub-skill described.

final_groups.skill_concept: Patching an existing Makefile to fix compiler identity or flags (including cross-compilation toolchain targets) and rebuilding with make
final_groups.reasoning: Both tasks start with a broken or wrong Makefile, require targeted sed/text edits to compiler variables and flags (one swapping ifort→gfortran with flag correction, the other adding a full MIPS LLVM/binutils toolchain block), and validate success by running make to produce the expected binary artifact.
